issues.title: Multi-value field widget table renders an empty <th> for the actions (Remove) column
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

Since Drupal 10.2 (#1038316), the table rendered for multi-value field widgets has a column for the per-item "Remove" button. The header cell for that column is an empty array, so it renders as an empty <th></th>.

In 11.x this is in \Drupal\Core\Field\FieldPreprocess::preprocessFieldMultipleValueForm() (previously template_preprocess_field_multiple_value_form()):

$header = [
  [
    'data' => [ /* h4 field label */ ],
    'colspan' => 2,
    'class' => ['field-label'],
  ],
  [],
  $this->t('Order', [], ['context' => 'Sort order']),
];

Accessibility checkers report an empty table header on every form with an unlimited/multi-value field: axe-core's empty-table-header rule and Editoria11y's "Empty table header" check. Screen reader users get no name for the column that holds the Remove buttons. This relates to WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.

#3587682 reported an empty table header from an automated scan, but it was closed as "cannot reproduce". That report pointed at a different page. This issue is the reproducible case in the field widget table.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Install Drupal with the Standard profile (Claro as the admin theme).
  2. Add a reference field (paragraph reference) with unlimited cardinality to the Article content type.
  3. Go to /node/add/article.
  4. Inspect the field's table header: the third <th> is empty.
  5. Run axe DevTools or Editoria11y on the page: it reports an empty table header.

Proposed resolution

Give the actions column header a visually hidden label so it has an accessible name without changing the visual design:

[
  'data' => [
    '#type' => 'html_tag',
    '#tag' => 'span',
    '#value' => $this->t('Operations'),
    '#attributes' => ['class' => ['visually-hidden']],
  ],
],

"Operations" matches the label core already uses for action columns elsewhere, such as entity list builders. Claro's preprocess_field_multiple_value_form keeps working: for disabled widgets, its loop adds the is-disabled class to header cells that have a data key.

Alternative: only output the column (header and cells) when at least one item has _actions. That also fixes the empty body cells contrib widgets get (see Paragraphs #3418303). It is a larger change and could be a follow-up.

Remaining tasks

  • Review the approach and the label wording.
  • Add test coverage that the header cell is not empty, e.g. in an existing multi-value widget functional test.
  • Convert to an MR.

User interface changes

No visual change. Screen readers announce the actions column header as "Operations".

API changes

None.

Data model changes

None.

Release notes snippet

N/A

Dialogs subtly jump into position after opening
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

While investigating #3631339: [random test failure] FieldTest::testModalDialogTitle fails intermittently, I found that Drupal dialogs first open at the wrong position, which is then corrected about 20ms later:

This fitted surprisingly well with a subconscious aversion to Drupal dialogs that I'd had for some time. Like an unexplainable, involuntary, autonomic reaction, something just felt off.

Now I can explain it, managed to capture the quite perceptible jump in a video, and we may now fix its cause.

While not reaching the three flashes threshold of WCAG 2.3.1/2.3.2, the abrupt repositioning is still distracting and may cause averse reactions in other users as well. Unnecessarily abrupt visual motion may even contribute to dizziness, nausea or headaches in motion-sensitive users, as described in Understanding SC 2.3.3.

Steps to reproduce

While not necessarily restricted to Views, to reproduce the issue please:

  1. Edit some view in Views UI.
  2. Scroll down and open some dialog.
  3. Notice (or film in slow-motion) the dialog first appearing too far down, then jumping upwards.

Proposed resolution

To remove the delayed initial resize, we need to calculate the dialog's size and position correctly before opening the dialog. Getting there however requires a few related bugfixes:

  1. Normalize numeric strings with or without "px" to numbers, and convert percentage heights to pixels.
  2. Normalize autoResize to a boolean after beforecreate listeners had a chance to modify it.
  3. Set position: fixed for dialogs with autoResize enabled before jQuery UI calculates the initial coordinates.
  4. Preserve positioning options that keep non-modal dialogs within the viewport.
  5. Retain autoResize update on viewport and displacement changes using the shared calculation methods.

To avoid regressions, expand our quite a bit lacking test coverage for dialog sizes and positions, including modal and non-modal dialogs, reopening, and option changes.

Remaining tasks

Accessibility and Javascript review.

User interface changes

None, besides dialogs opening at their correct position immediately:

Introduced terminology

None.

API changes

None.

Data model changes

None.

Release notes snippet

Dialogs no longer jump into position after opening.

comments.author: pancho
comments.body_html:
Ready for review. This should also resolve #3631339: [random test failure] FieldTest::testModalDialogTitle fails intermittently.

The underlying problems in unpatched Core are:

In unpatched Core, jQuery UI first positions the dialog with position: absolute.
It's only after the dialog has already opened that Drupal's autoResize code changes it to position: fixed, however without recalculating its coordinates. On a scrolled page, this can put the dialog too far down, potentially leaving its title outside the viewport. A delayed correction then makes the dialog jump into position.

Dialogs with percentage-based height

The delayed resizing corrects the position by triggering _position(), but only after the dialog has already opened. This makes the dialog jump into position, for both modal and non-modal dialogs.

Dialogs with numeric height

With a numeric maxHeight, the delayed resize does not perform the percentage conversion nor the appropriate position correction.
Additional problem is: after the AJAX round trip, the height value reaches our JS as the string "400" and is passed as such to jQuery UI, which explicitly checks its typeof and then discards the value rather than silently converting it into 400.
And as resetPosition() replaces the position options without preserving collision: 'fit', the top of an oversized non-modal dialog can move outside the viewport. Views UI normally uses 95%, but numeric sizes are relevant for other callers.

Resulting random test failures

For modal dialogs, there is another consequence: bodyScrollLock.lock() sets overflow: hidden on the root element. The misplaced title can then be clipped outside the viewport, so ChromeDriver treats it as hidden. getText() may return an empty string, while waitForElementVisible() may time out.
This may explain the intermittent failures in #3631339: [random test failure] FieldTest::testModalDialogTitle fails intermittently, when the test checks the title before the delayed correction happens. The timing differences between sometimes failing CI runs and mostly passing local test runs are not yet fully understood.

This MR converts the requested sizes and sets fixed positioning before jQuery UI calculates the initial coordinates, preserving collision handling. Dialogs now open at their intended size and position, without needing the delayed initial correction. autoResize updates when the viewport or Drupal displacement offsets change remain supported.

comments.body_html:
Stephen,

yes, as I already explained when you last asked me, I do use AI for assistance. But no, it's not written by AI. I do take responsibility for every single word I chose and every deficit I overlooked.

Coming from the flaky tests issue, I have, however, put hours over hours – including a whole sleepless night – into thoroughly investigating this problem, analyzing ChromeDriver's behaviour, confirming and documenting the UI bug in practice, developing a quick fix, expanding it into a proper, thorough solution, making sure all relevant scenarios are properly taken care of, and expanding the test coverage.

Being confronted with yet another gotcha question about AI, without any concrete concern about the contribution itself, is disheartening. I may be on the more verbose side, but I think the level of detail is warranted by the complexity of this issue. Whenever my issue summaries for rather obvious tasks or fixes are on the shorter side, such as in:

  • #3633353: Remove redundant render context lookup in Renderer::doRender(), or
  • #3634152: preprocessBlock() documentation describes obsolete behaviour and properties,

you're not ok with it either.

I've tried to take it in good humour, but that's getting increasingly difficult.

If there's something wrong with my explanation, design decisions, technical scope, implementation or test coverage, I'm very happy to discuss it. That's the feedback I'm hoping for and that I would find most helpful. Just tell me what's wrong and I'll fix it and learn from the constructive criticism.

But you'll understand that I value my time, my work and particularly my dignity too much to just keep playing gotcha games. I'd rather take some time off.

Inline form error summary link is broken on textarea/textfield widgets
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

When inline_form_errors is enabled, there is a summary that is displayed at the top of the page in a status message, when the form has field errors.

It is supposed to contain anchor links to the relevant fields, for the user to click on and correct the error.

However, on the text_textarea and text_textfield widgets, the anchor link is broken. It links to #edit-foobar-0, which is an ID that doesn't exist on the page, instead of #edit-foobar-0-value, which is the actual form field element.

The root cause is that the errorElement function on those widgets doesn't point to the proper form value element.

Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure that inline_form_errors is enabled.
2. Create a text or text_long field to a node bundle.
3. Add a constraint to the field definition on the bundle.
4. Create and save a node with a value that triggers a constraint validation error on the field.
5. Note that the link in the error summary status message does not work.

Proposed resolution

Update the errorElement function to point to value.

issues.title: The active primary local task has a too low color contrast and shapeshifting compared to the active secondary local task
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

I've opened that issue already over in the Gin queue: https://git.drupalcode.org/project/gin/-/work_items/3506311. Over the course of the last few days I was able to slowly catch up again after being out of the loop for the last few months except for my attendance in the weekly ux meetings.

The styling of primary and secondary local tasks in the Default Admin Theme has two main problems:

  1. Color contrast wise, it is not meeting WCAG2.2 SC1.4.11
  2. You have shapeshifting objects, which means the same objects, tabs in this case, that are looking completely different. Active primary tabs have a chip or button-like styling, while the non-active tabs are not visually connected; they are just connected by proximity. The secondary tab has a familiar design for tabs with a strong bottom border for the active secondary tab and a barely visible light thin bottom border connecting all the available secondary tabs.

That way the overall cognitive load is high:

Steps to reproduce

Proposed resolution

Make sure that the chip for the active primary local task has a color contrast of at least 3:1 against the background in light and dark mode. issues.title: The active accent color is not communicated
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

If you are getting to admin/appearance/settings/default_admin the active accent color is not apparent. In Safari you also don't see any outline at all for the active accent color when you are changing it (safari.mp4), while in Edge and Firefox you see an outline after you have selected and clicked your new desired accent color (edge.mp4, firefox.mp4). But that outline is hidden again in those two browsers as soon as you are changing any other setting on the page by click.

Steps to reproduce

Go to admin/appearance/settings/default_admin and try to figure out which of the accent color circles is the active one.

Proposed resolution

Show an outline for the active accent color persistently.

Introduced terminology

Data model changes

comments.author: rkoller
comments.body_html:
thank you for working on the issue @leandro713! I've quickly tested the MR manually, and there a few details ive noticed:

The MR is introducing a light greyish outline in dark mode and a darkish outline in light mode. Two things I wonder about in this context. First the width of the persistent outline is thinner compared to the outline you get on focus/on click (outline.mp4). And this MR would be introducing another color to communicate state. So far selections like for example for the layout density on the very same page is communicated by the accent color. I am well aware that the color for the outline for the selection would have the very same color as the circle that is selected, but there is still a padding/gap between the outline for the active option and the selected option itself. personally i would vote to have the same, thicker, width for the persistent selection outline. in regard of the color choice i am not sure. i just wanted to raise that potential inconsistency for discussion.

When you interact with the component by keyboard as soon as you move the select to the left or right you are unable to see what the current setting is/was, so the user has to remember that previous choice (keyboard.mp4).

comments.author: leandro713
comments.body_html:
@rkroller:
Thanks for the review. I understand the keyboard concern now: the persistent indicator was tied to :checked, so it moved as the radio selection changed with the arrow keys. I’ve updated it to keep marking the initially checked accent while leaving the focus indicator on the focused option. I’ve also made the persistent ring the same thickness as the focus ring and used the accent color to better match the other selected controls.

In relation to the TAB movement with the keyboard, now the persistent indicator is tied to the radio button’s initial checked attribute rather than its dynamic :checked state. This keeps the accent saved when the form loads visibly marked while keyboard navigation moves focus between options. The existing focus indicator continues to show which option currently has focus, so users can distinguish the saved accent from the option they are navigating to. After the form is saved and reloaded, the newly saved accent becomes the initially checked option and receives the persistent indicator.

@kentr:
Yes, I used an LLM to help reason through the CSS approach and the review feedback. I reviewed the change and tested it manually, and I take responsibility for the MR.
